lesson.title: Morning Focus, Afternoon Workshop: Design Your Learning Day
lesson.topic: Plan a day with focused academics (math, reading, writing) in the morning and hands-on workshops or projects in the afternoon.
lesson.steelman: Should hard thinking come first in the day, or should a learner start with what they love?
lesson.steelman_for: Most people focus best earlier, and saving hands-on work for the afternoon gives energy a place to go when attention dips.
lesson.steelman_against: Not every learner peaks in the morning, and a rigid split can cut off a project right when curiosity is high.
lesson.example: Imagine Mia, 9, who does math and reading from 9 to 11:30, eats lunch, and then spends the afternoon building a birdhouse and practicing guitar. She notices she finishes math faster when it comes first.
lesson.activity: Draw tomorrow as a two-column plan: Morning Focus (2-3 academic blocks with short breaks) and Afternoon Workshop (one hands-on project or skill). Try it for one day, then circle what worked.
check_questions: What goes in a Morning Focus block?
Why might a hands-on workshop work well after lunch?
What would you change about your plan after trying it once?
